Find the area bounded between the curve $x=\frac{1}{3}{y}^{2}+2y,$ the $y$-axis, and the lines $y=0$ and $y=2,$ as shown above.
feedback.worked_solution:
To find the area, we compute the corresponding definite integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\int }_{c}^{d}x(y)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}(\frac{1}{3}{y}^{2}+2y)\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{\int }_{0}^{2}{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y+2{\int }_{0}^{2}y\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\cdot {\frac{{y}^{3}}{3}|}_{0}^{2}+2\cdot {\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}|}_{0}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}(\frac{8}{3}-0)+2(2-0) \\  & =\frac{8}{9}+4 \\  & =\frac{44}{9}\end{aligned}
$$
